question: In case of a drastic change in niches of organisms, which of the following can save the population of an organism from getting completely wiped out?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Variation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Variation** refers to the differences in characteristics or traits among individuals of a species.
 
• These variations can be genetic, arising from mutations, gene recombination, and other hereditary factors.
 
• Organisms with beneficial variations are more likely to survive and reproduce in changing environments.
 
• This ability to adapt through variation provides a buffer against drastic changes in niches, preventing the species from getting wiped out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Selection:**

 
 
• It is the process where organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring.
 
• This concept was introduced by Charles Darwin and is a key mechanism of evolution.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Drift:**
 
 
• It is a mechanism of evolution that refers to random changes in the frequency of alleles in a gene pool.
 
• Genetic drift can result in the loss of genetic variation within populations.
 
 
 
• **Mutation:**
 
 
• A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence of an organism's genome.
 
• Mutations can introduce new genetic variations and are a source of genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Gene Flow:**
 
 
• Gene flow is the transfer of genetic material from one population to another.
 
• It can increase genetic variation within a population and reduce differences between populations.
